exposure: General anesthesia vs. regional anesthesia during Cesarean delivery
Deferred cord clamping (DCC) duration (>= 60s vs. shorter)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 170 mothers and 194 preterm infants born at less than 33 weeks gestation via Cesarean delivery between January 2018 and December 2023.
finding: Deferred cord clamping (DCC) for 60 seconds or more was associated with improved maternal outcomes (less blood loss, transfusions) and neonatal outcomes (less DR resuscitation, chronic lung disease, higher survival without major morbidities), while general anesthesia during Cesarean delivery had mixed associations with neonatal acid-base status and necrotizing enterocolitis.
mod_finding: General anesthesia with deferred cord clamping during Cesarean deliveries was not associated with increased neonatal resuscitation or major neonatal morbidities and was linked to lower maternal hemorrhage and transfusion.
